question: What is the primary clinical definition of faecal incontinence?

options.A: The inability to produce bowel movements for over a week
options.B: The recurrent involuntary passage of faecal material
options.C: The excessive production of intestinal gas causing abdominal distension
options.D: Painful defecation accompanied by bright red rectal bleeding

explanation: Faecal incontinence specifically refers to the loss of voluntary control over the evacuation of bowel contents. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why is faecal incontinence often underreported by patients presenting to healthcare facilities?

options.A: Rapid resolution of symptoms without medical intervention
options.C: Lack of available diagnostic tools in local clinics
options.D: Strict hospital policies limiting symptom discussion

explanation: Patients frequently hide bowel control issues due to the sensitive nature of the topic and fear of social ostracization. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h1)

question: Which muscle forms a sling around the anorectal junction to maintain the acute anococcygeal angle?
explanation: The puborectalis muscle acts as a mechanical sling, pulling the rectum forward to maintain continence at rest. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h2)

question: What is the primary function of the internal anal sphincter?

options.A: Secreting mucus to lubricate the lower anal canal
options.B: Providing voluntary squeezing during emergency defection
options.C: Detecting the chemical composition of passing gas
options.D: Maintaining resting anal tone through involuntary control

explanation: The internal anal sphincter is a smooth muscle that stays contracted continuously to prevent leakage when resting. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h2)

question: What is a leading cause of faecal incontinence among women in many Nigerian clinical settings?

options.A: Idiopathic degeneration of the descending colon
options.C: Obstetric trauma from prolonged obstructed labor
options.D: Chronic use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs

explanation: Difficult childbirths with perineal trauma or delayed medical interventions frequently damage the anal sphincter complex. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h3)

question: How do neurological conditions such as stroke contribute to the development of faecal incontinence?

options.A: By directly destroying the smooth muscle fibers of the rectal wall
options.B: By disrupting central nervous system control over bowel evacuation reflexes
options.C: By halting all mucus production within the large intestine
options.D: By causing permanent hyper-contraction of the internal anal sphincter

explanation: Stroke and spinal injuries impair the neural pathways required for conscious awareness and voluntary control of defecation. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h3)

question: What characterizes passive faecal incontinence compared to urge incontinence?

options.A: Leakage occurs without the patient's conscious awareness
options.B: The patient experiences an intense, sudden urge to defecate
options.C: It is exclusively caused by acute bacterial infections
options.D: Symptoms only appear during strenuous physical exercise

explanation: Passive incontinence happens when sensory nerves fail to signal rectal filling or sphincters fail silently due to severe weakness. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h4)

question: A patient feels a sudden, urgent need to defecate but leaks stool before reaching the toilet. What type of incontinence is this?
explanation: This scenario describes urge incontinence, where the warning is felt, but the sphincter mechanism is too weak to hold back stool. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h4)

question: What is the clinical purpose of assessing the anal wink reflex during a physical examination?

options.A: To determine the moisture level of the perineal skin
options.B: To detect the presence of internal hemorrhoids
options.C: To evaluate the integrity of the S2-S4 sacral reflex arc
options.D: To measure the exact resting pressure of the internal sphincter

explanation: Stroking the perianal skin normally causes a reflex contraction of the external sphincter, proving intact sacral innervation. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h5)

question: Which tool is most appropriate for a nurse to use when assessing and recording a patient's stool consistency?
explanation: The Bristol Stool Chart classifies human stool forms into seven distinct categories, aiding clinical communication regarding consistency. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h5)

question: What physiological mechanism is utilized when scheduling bowel training after meals?
explanation: Eating triggers the gastrocolic reflex, which naturally increases colon motility and facilitates scheduled bowel evacuation. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h6)

question: A patient undergoing pelvic floor muscle training for faecal incontinence keeps squeezing their buttocks and holding their breath. What is the appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Advise the patient to increase the weight resistance during the contraction phase
options.B: Switch the treatment plan immediately to commercial bulk-forming laxatives
options.C: Document that the patient has completed the pelvic floor exercise routine successfully
options.D: Correct the technique by instructing the patient to isolate the anal and perineal muscles

explanation: Effective pelvic floor training requires isolating the sphincter and puborectalis muscles rather than recruiting gluteal or abdominal muscles. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h6)

question: What is the primary cause of perineal dermatitis in patients with faecal incontinence?

options.A: Irritation from fecal enzymes and prolonged moisture exposure
options.B: Fungal overgrowth caused by systemic antibiotic therapy
options.C: Mechanical friction from frequent ambulatory exercise
options.D: Allergic reactions to standard hospital-issued cotton linen

explanation: Enzymes present in stool combined with constant moisture breakdown the skin barrier, leading to painful inflammation and breakdown. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h7)

question: Why is it clinically recommended to pat dry rather than rub the perianal skin after cleansing?

options.A: To prevent the barrier ointment from sliding off the area
options.B: To ensure the skin absorbs residual moisture more rapidly
options.C: To avoid causing mechanical friction and further skin breakdown
options.D: To stimulate local blood circulation in the subcutaneous tissue

explanation: Fragile, macerated skin is highly susceptible to frictional damage, making gentle patting essential during hygiene care. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h7)

question: Which psychosocial challenge is most commonly reported by individuals living with chronic faecal incontinence?
explanation: Fear of accidental soilage and embarrassment often drives patients to withdraw socially, leading to profound emotional distress. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h8)

question: What is an effective nursing intervention to help manage the emotional impact of faecal incontinence?

options.A: Encouraging the patient to avoid all public outings indefinitely
options.B: Insisting that family members take over all personal hygiene tasks
options.C: Minimizing discussion of the topic to prevent further embarrassment
options.D: Creating a safe, non-judgmental space for open communication

explanation: Validating the patient's feelings and offering a compassionate environment helps reduce stigma and encourages adherence to care plans. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h8)
